clue.text: Exercises dodges as scrutineer does

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school exercises
ruses are tricks or dodges

explanation.surface: Someone checking votes keeps fit and ducks out of things.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrutineer examines ballots closely, which is reading through them carefully.

clue.text: Exerting unfair influence in drawing part of orchestra

parts.note: drawing a cart is hauling or pulling it
the violins, violas, cellos and basses form the strings section

explanation.surface: A musician bribes the conductor while sketching a section of the band.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes using secret influence, like a puppeteer working hidden cords.

clue.text: Copy the material on Tom in fiction

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric

indicators.note: the word in tells us the tom is placed inside the word for fiction

parts.note: a lie is a fiction or falsehood
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: Reproduce the fabric worn by a character named Tom in a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom is not a person here: a tom is a male CAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To replicate something is to duplicate or reproduce it exactly.

clue.text: Express indifference with a joint movement

definitions.text: Express indifference with a joint movement

parts.words: Express indifference with a joint movement
parts.note: the gesture of not caring made by lifting the shoulder joints, with joint also hinting at shared action

explanation.surface: Two people jointly signal that they could not care less.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising and dropping the shoulders is the classic bodily gesture of not caring.

clue.text: Ad led desk to get confused -quick flight perhaps?

indicators.note: letters that get confused are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: An advertisement leads the desk into chaos, followed by a hasty exit.
explanation.definitionFit: Skedaddle, as a noun, means a hurried departure or running off in haste.

clue.text: The failure's gone off, showing resentment

parts.note: a dud is a failure, the 's being a link

indicators.note: gone off suggests these letters have gone bad and been rearranged

explanation.surface: A flop has gone sour, and it shows in someone's bitter mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' turns GONE into GEON after DUD.
explanation.definitionFit: Dudgeon is a feeling of deep offence or indignation, as in 'high dudgeon'.

clue.text: Put in order for formal clothing

explanation.surface: Arrange things neatly before putting on evening wear.
explanation.definitionFit: To align troops in ranks is a military sense; a gown or frock is a formal garment.

clue.text: Rash deed rival misrepresented

indicators.note: something misrepresented is shown wrongly, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A competitor's reckless action has been falsely portrayed.
explanation.definitionFit: A daredevil person is reckless, taking foolhardy risks, so the word works as an adjective.

clue.text: Celt's heart is with the spirit in Scottish town

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letters

parts.note: gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A Celtic drinker's core is in a Scottish town with gin.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of CELT is its middle pair, EL.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgin is a town in Moray, in north-east Scotland.

clue.text: It's normal with study of dates that can be seen in a museum

definitions.text: that can be seen in a museum

parts.note: natural means normal or ordinary
history is the study of past events and their dates

explanation.surface: A display of ordinary things combined with dates is on show in a museum.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to London's Natural History Museum.
explanation.definitionFit: London's famous museum of dinosaurs and fossils takes its name from this branch of science.

clue.text: One despised to drive away to the west

indicators.note: in an across clue, going west means reading from right to left

parts.note: to repel is to drive away

explanation.surface: An outcast is chased off towards the west.
explanation.definitionFit: A leper, figuratively, is a person shunned or rejected by society.

clue.text: Look at the intelligent little bloomer!

parts.note: to eye something is to look at it
bright means clever or intelligent

explanation.surface: Gaze at the clever youngster who has made a small mistake!
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is British slang for a blunder, but here it is a plant that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A small wild flower of the genus Euphrasia, once used to treat sore eyes.

clue.text: One fault by the tumbler and a sort of gelatine is required

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a sin is a fault or wrongdoing
a tumbler is a drinking glass

explanation.surface: A single flaw in the drinking vessel calls for some jelly to fix it.
explanation.definitionFit: Isinglass is a pure gelatine got from fish bladders, used in jellies and for clarifying beer.

clue.text: Giver of name to be put in the entrance

indicators.note: put in tells us one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: a door is an entrance

explanation.surface: Whoever gave the gift should have their name placed at the doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor is a benefactor who gives money, blood or organs.

clue.text: Good fabric with a glossy finish

parts.note: lace is a delicate openwork fabric

explanation.surface: A fine material with a shiny surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Glacé describes leather or cloth given a smooth, shiny surface, or fruit candied to shine.

clue.text: A physical phenomenon I have found to be viable

parts.note: an effect such as the Doppler effect is a physical phenomenon
I have shortens to I've

explanation.surface: A scientist says a phenomenon they've discovered can work.
explanation.definitionFit: Something workable and capable of producing results is said to be viable.

clue.text: Denial of knowledge of laws and avoid being in trouble

indicators.note: letters in trouble are in disarray, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker claims ignorance of the rules and dodges getting into difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A disavowal is a refusal to acknowledge something, a repudiation or disclaiming.

clue.text: Words from play to team outside the play area

indicators.note: the word to says the first piece is added to the team's word

parts.note: a side is a team
an actor's lines are words from a play

explanation.surface: Script extracts are handed to a team standing beyond the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: The sidelines are the boundary lines of a pitch and the area just beyond them.

clue.text: Plain to see, trail grew very obscure

indicators.note: letters made very obscure are scrambled out of recognition

explanation.surface: A path became ever harder to make out.
explanation.definitionFit: Writ large means in an obvious, magnified or exaggerated form.

clue.text: He's organised c-contestants in the city

indicators.note: organised suggests these letters are set out in a new order

parts.note: the stutter on the clue word tells us to stutter its synonym too: contestants are a field, said with its first letter repeated

explanation.surface: A man arranges stammering competitors in an urban centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' turns HES into SHE. The printed stutter 'c-contestants' asks for its synonym FIELD stuttered the same way, F-FIELD.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheffield is a major city in South Yorkshire, England, famous for steel.

clue.text: See 1
Scottish port: some stock pile it habitually

indicators.note: some of the following words supplies the letters running through them

explanation.surface: In a Scottish harbour, goods are always heaped up.
explanation.definitionFit: Leith is the port district of Edinburgh on the Firth of Forth.

clue.text: See 8
Priest in the right cape, an object of historic interest

indicators.note: in tells us the priest's name goes inside the other letters

parts.note: C is the map abbreviation for cape
Eli is the biblical priest who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A priest wearing the proper cloak is himself something of an antique.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli is the priest of Shiloh in the Book of Samuel, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is something surviving from the past, kept for its historical value.

clue.text: Abatement in dispute lord brought up

indicators.note: brought up says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A lessening in a quarrel raised by a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's parse stands; 'in' is added as the hiding indicator it plainly is. In a down clue 'brought up' reads PUTEL from the bottom upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A let-up is a pause or reduction in intensity, a slackening.

clue.text: Boring places?

parts.note: not dull spots but sites where drilling or boring into the ground goes on, for crude

explanation.surface: Dull locations nobody wants to visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' wants to mean dull; it means drilling.
explanation.definitionFit: Petroleum-producing areas are where wells are drilled into the earth.

clue.text: Give a view round the tree

parts.note: O is round in shape
a pine is a tree

explanation.surface: Offer an opinion about the tree nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to state an opinion or express a belief.

clue.text: To suffer, being caught in catastrophic ruin

indicators.note: in shows the abbreviation for caught is placed inside the jumbled letters
catastrophic suggests these letters are wrecked and rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: To endure being trapped in a disastrous collapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catastrophic' turns RUIN into INUR, and 'in' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur a loss or penalty is to bring it upon oneself and undergo it.

clue.text: Food unit with rot in cracks

indicators.note: cracks, as a verb, means these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A food container goes bad as decay gets into its splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutrition is nourishment, the food needed for health and growth.

clue.text: What's loaded as vehicle set off

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
to go is to set off or depart

explanation.surface: The goods are on board as the truck pulls away.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is the freight or goods carried by a ship, plane or lorry.

clue.text: Excellent drink with army unit

parts.note: to sup is to drink
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A soldier rates having a drink with his regiment as first-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: REME is the British Army's Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme means highest in quality or degree, outstanding.

clue.text: Church in sad spell

indicators.note: in tells us the church abbreviation is set inside the word for sad

parts.note: sorry means sad or regretful
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church goes through an unhappy period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spell' looks like a period of time; it is magic.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorcery is witchcraft, the casting of magical charms.
